paper.title: Parcae: Scaling Laws For Stable Looped Language Models
paper.abstract: Traditional fixed-depth architectures scale quality by increasing training FLOPs, typically through increased parameterization, at the expense of a higher memory footprint, or data. A potential alternative is looped architectures, which instead increase FLOPs by sending activations through a block of layers in a loop. While promising, existing recipes for training looped architectures can be unstable, suffering from residual explosion and loss spikes. We address these challenges by recasting loo

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文解决的是 looped language model 的两个核心障碍：一是训练不稳定，表现为 residual state 爆炸和 loss spikes；二是即便 looped 架构在参数效率上有吸引力，也缺少像参数规模、数据规模那样可预测的 scaling law，因此很难把“循环深度”当成一个可靠的计算扩展轴。作者的目标不是单纯把已有 recurrent-depth 模型训稳，而是把 looping 从一个脆弱技巧，变成可分析、可训练、可做训练与测试时计算扩展的体系。
summary.importance: 这项工作对预训练研究的意义比较直接，而且量级不小。它触及一个很现实的问题：如果未来部署成本越来越受参数量和 KV/cache 内存约束，那么“增加 FLOPs 但不增加参数”会成为重要方向。looped / recurrent-depth 模型正好提供了这条路，但过去一直卡在稳定性和 recipe 不可靠。Parcae 的贡献有三层。第一，它给出了一个解释 instability 的分析框架，把 looped Transformer 写成 residual stream 上的动力系统，并把问题收敛到 injection 参数的谱范数。第二，它提出了结构约束和训练算法修正，使 1.3B、100B token 量级的训练变得稳定。第三，它给出 looping 的训练 FLOP scaling law 和 test-time scaling law，说明循环深度可以像参数和数据一样成为独立扩展轴。这一点对 pretrain 设计空间很重要，因为它意味着 compute-optimal 配方不一定只能在参数和数据之间分配，还可以在“重复计算同一块”上分配。
summary.technical_approach:
技术路线分成三部分：稳定性建模、稳定架构设计、以及面向随机深度训练的算法修正。

先看建模。作者把 middle-looped 架构写成三段：prelude 单元把输入 token 映射成条件向量 e，recurrent unit 在循环步 t 上更新 hidden state h_t，coda 单元把最终状态映射到 logits。关键是把 recurrent update 视为一个关于 residual stream 的非线性时变系统，其中一部分参数控制“保留多少旧状态、注入多少新状态”。在对系统做线性化近似后，这个更新退化成经典 LTI 系统，稳定性可以用状态转移矩阵的谱性质来分析。作者发现，已有 looped 架构中的 injection 参数会学到过大的谱范数，从而导致 residual explosion。这不是经验上“有时会炸”，而是能被动力系统视角解释的结构性风险。

基于这个分析，Parcae 的核心设计是对 A 做连续到离散的稳定参数化，并把连续形式的 A 约束为 negative diagonal matrix。这样离散化后的状态更新天然带有收缩性质，谱范数被控制住，残差不会在循环中指数放大。这个设计很像把 recurrent depth 的自由度从“任意线性耦合”收缩到“逐维稳定衰减/保留”，牺牲了一部分表达灵活性，换来训练稳定性和可预测性。作者没有选择更宽松的全矩阵稳定化，而是用对角负矩阵，原因很实际：它足够稳定、参数少、实现简单，而且在大模型训练里更容易和现有 Transformer block 兼容。

除了结构约束，作者还处理了两个训练层面的尖点来源。第一，对输入条件 e 做归一化，缓解训练后期的 loss spikes。这里可以理解为 recurrent unit 在不同 loop depth 下反复接收同一个条件信号，如果其尺度漂移，容易在深循环时放大不稳定模式。第二，训练目标需要对随机深度的期望损失做优化。已有做法常在 batch 级别采样统一深度，导致梯度方差和深度切换带来的不连续更明显。Parcae 改成 intra-batch per-sequence depth sampling，让同一 batch 内不同样本走不同 loop 次数，从而平滑优化过程，也更接近“对深度分布求期望”的目标。

论文还有一个重要点是把训练时 scaling 和测试时 scaling 统一起来。训练时，他们在 isoFLOP 设定下研究给定总训练 FLOPs 时，应该把预算分给更多数据还是更多 looping；测试时，他们研究增加 loop 次数带来的 loss 改善曲线，并拟合出带 irreducible loss 的指数衰减形式。最终得到一个统一的 looping scaling 视角：训练阶段学到的 recurrent refinement 能在推理阶段继续通过更多循环释放出来，但收益遵循可预测的递减规律。
summary.experiments:
实验分成稳定性、端到端质量、训练 FLOP scaling、测试时 scaling 四块。

稳定性方面，作者先证明旧配方确实容易出现 residual explosion 和 loss spikes，并把问题和 injection 参数的谱范数联系起来。Table 2 是关键证据之一：不稳定模型会学到更危险的 A 参数化，而 Parcae 的约束能显著抑制这种现象。文中还强调，过去一些 looped 模型往往依赖敏感超参和 Post-Norm 才能勉强收敛，Parcae 则把稳定性更多前移到参数化本身。

端到端质量方面，Parcae 与参数量、数据量匹配的 RDMs 和标准 Transformer 比较。结果上，相比 RDM，验证集 perplexity 降低 6.3%。当规模扩展到 1.3B 参数、100B tokens 时，Parcae 在 Core 和 Core-Extended benchmark 上分别比参数匹配 Transformer 高最多 2.99 和 1.18 分，并能匹配约两倍参数量的 Transformer。这是全文最重要的结果之一，因为它说明 looping 不是只在 toy setting 下省参数，而是在较实在的预训练规模上也能换到质量。

训练 FLOP scaling 方面，作者做了 parameter-matched isoFLOP 实验：总训练 FLOPs 固定时，比较把预算用于更多数据，还是用于更多 loop depth。结论是 looping 构成了与参数、数据并列的独立 scaling 轴，最优配方会同时增加数据和 looping，并满足经验幂律。Figure 1 右图是这里的核心图。这个结果的含义不是“looping 总比数据好”，而是“在固定参数下，compute-optimal 解不只是一味加数据”。

测试时 scaling 方面，作者观察到增加循环次数会带来可预测的 loss 下降，形式接近指数衰减并存在不可约下界。也就是说，模型确实学会了可继续 refinement 的动态，但额外 loop 的边际收益会越来越小。论文进一步把训练期和测试期的 scaling law 合在一起，形成统一拟合。这一点对部署很关键，因为它支持按场景做 per-token 或 per-request 的计算分配。

从全文叙述看，消融实验还覆盖了 A 的参数化方式、e normalization、以及 per-sequence depth sampling 对 loss spikes 的影响。值得注意的是，作者不是只报告最终分数，而是把训练曲线稳定性本身当成一等结果来分析，这对做大规模预训练的人更有参考价值。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇建议精读。最值得看的不是 benchmark 表，而是作者如何把 looped Transformer 重新表述成动力系统，以及这个表述如何直接导出可训练的参数化。

阅读顺序建议如下。先看 Introduction，把问题框住：为什么 looped model 值得做，过去卡在哪里。然后直接看 Background 里 middle-looped architecture 的形式化定义，确保符号 e、h_t、P/R/C 三段结构都看明白。接着重点读稳定性分析部分，尤其是从非线性时变系统线性化到 LTI 的那一步，以及为什么谱范数会控制残差爆炸。这里是全文的理论支点。之后看 Parcae 的参数化设计：连续 A、离散化、negative diagonal constraint。再看训练算法修正，包括 e normalization 和 intra-batch per-sequence depth sampling。最后看三组实验：Table 2 的稳定性证据、Figure 1 的 scaling law、以及 1.3B/100B token 的主结果表。

几个值得深挖的点。第一，negative diagonal A 很稳，但表达能力是否受限，未来是否可以做更丰富但仍稳定的低秩或块对角参数化。第二，test-time scaling 的指数衰减说明 recurrent refinement 有“可榨取但有限”的剩余计算空间，这和 latent reasoning、adaptive compute、early exit 都有联系。第三，训练时随机深度分布如何选，可能会显著影响模型在不同推理预算下的 Pareto 曲线，这里还有不少可做空间。第四，这项工作和传统 AR Transformer 不是替代关系，更像在固定参数预算下增加一个 compute 维度；如果和 MoE、长上下文、speculative decoding 联合考虑，系统层面的最优点可能会变。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper tackles two bottlenecks in looped language models. First, training is often unstable, with residual-state explosion and late-stage loss spikes. Second, even when looping is parameter-efficient, it has lacked the kind of predictable scaling behavior that makes parameter count and data size useful design axes. The goal is therefore broader than “make recurrence work”: it is to turn looping into a stable and analyzable compute-scaling mechanism for language model pretraining.
summary_en.importance: This is directly relevant to pretraining research. If deployment is increasingly constrained by parameter memory and inference footprint, then scaling quality through extra FLOPs without extra parameters becomes attractive. Looped or recurrent-depth models are a natural candidate, but prior recipes have been fragile. Parcae contributes at three levels. It provides a dynamical-systems explanation for instability, tying divergence to the spectral norm of injection parameters. It introduces a stable architecture and training recipe that works at meaningful scale, including 1.3B parameters and 100B tokens. And it derives training-time and test-time scaling laws for looping, arguing that recurrent depth can serve as an orthogonal scaling axis alongside parameters and data. That is a meaningful expansion of the pretraining design space.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The technical story has three parts: stability analysis, stable parameterization, and training-algorithm fixes for stochastic depth.

The model is written as a middle-looped architecture with a prelude module, a recurrent middle block, and a coda module. The recurrent update over the residual stream is cast as a nonlinear time-varying dynamical system. After linearization, the update reduces to a linear time-invariant system, which makes classical stability analysis available. The key empirical observation is that prior looped architectures can learn unstable injection operators with large spectral norms, leading to residual explosion.

Parcae addresses this by parameterizing the continuous-time state matrix A and discretizing it in a controlled way, while constraining A to be a negative diagonal matrix. This gives the recurrent update an inherently contractive character and prevents the hidden state from blowing up across loop iterations. The design is deliberately conservative: a diagonal stable parameterization gives up some flexibility relative to a full matrix, but it is simple, cheap, and robust enough for large-scale Transformer training.

The paper also identifies two practical sources of loss spikes. First, the conditioning signal e is repeatedly injected across loop steps, so scale drift in e can destabilize deep recurrence. Parcae adds normalization on e to mitigate this. Second, the training objective optimizes expected loss over variable depths. Prior recipes often sample one depth per batch, which creates higher variance and sharper optimization discontinuities. Parcae instead uses intra-batch per-sequence depth sampling, so different sequences in the same batch use different loop counts. This better matches the expectation-over-depth objective and empirically smooths training.

A further strength of the paper is that it connects training-time and inference-time scaling. Under isoFLOP training, it studies how compute should be split between more data and more looping. At test time, it studies how additional loop iterations reduce loss, finding an exponential-decay form with an irreducible floor. The result is a unified view in which recurrence learned during training can be exploited at inference, but with predictable diminishing returns.
summary_en.experiments:
The experiments cover stability, end-to-end quality, training-FLOP scaling, and test-time scaling.

On stability, the paper shows that earlier looped recipes indeed suffer from residual explosion and loss spikes, and links this behavior to the learned spectral properties of the injection operator. Table 2 is central here: unstable models learn more dangerous parameterizations, while Parcae’s constrained form suppresses that failure mode. An important practical point is that prior looped models often relied on sensitive hyperparameters and normalization choices such as Post-Norm just to converge; Parcae moves much of the stability burden into the parameterization itself.

On end-to-end quality, Parcae is compared against parameter- and data-matched RDMs and standard Transformers. Relative to RDMs, it reduces validation perplexity by 6.3%. At 1.3B parameters trained on 100B tokens, it outperforms parameter-matched Transformers by up to 2.99 points on Core and 1.18 points on Core-Extended, while matching Transformers roughly twice as large. That is the headline result: looping is not only a toy parameter-saving trick, but can buy real quality at meaningful pretraining scale.

For training-FLOP scaling, the paper runs parameter-matched isoFLOP studies and asks whether extra compute should go into more data or more loop depth. The answer is that looping behaves like an additional scaling axis. FLOP-optimal training increases both data and looping according to empirical power laws. The implication is not that looping dominates data, but that under a fixed parameter budget, the compute-optimal solution is not exhausted by “just add more tokens.”

For test-time scaling, increasing the number of loop iterations yields predictable loss improvements that follow an exponential decay toward an irreducible floor. This suggests that the model learns a genuine iterative refinement process, but one with diminishing returns. The paper then combines training-time and test-time fits into a unified scaling-law view. That is especially relevant for adaptive inference and per-request compute allocation.

The ablations also examine the parameterization of A, normalization of e, and the effect of per-sequence depth sampling on loss spikes. Importantly, the paper treats training-curve stability itself as a first-class result, which makes it more useful for practitioners than papers that only report final benchmark scores.
summary_en.reading_guide:
This one is worth a close read. The most important part is not the benchmark table but the way the paper reformulates looped Transformers as dynamical systems and then turns that analysis into a trainable architecture.

A good reading order is: Introduction, then the formal definition of the middle-looped architecture in the background section, then the stability analysis. Pay special attention to the step from the nonlinear time-varying system to the linearized LTI view, and to why the spectral norm governs residual explosion. That is the conceptual core of the paper. After that, read the Parcae parameterization carefully: continuous A, discretization, and the negative-diagonal constraint. Then read the training fixes, especially e normalization and intra-batch per-sequence depth sampling. Finally, study three experimental anchors: the stability evidence in Table 2, the scaling-law plots in Figure 1, and the main 1.3B / 100B-token quality results.

Several follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind. The negative-diagonal parameterization is stable, but perhaps restrictive; future work could explore low-rank or block-diagonal stable forms. The exponential test-time scaling curve suggests a finite but usable reserve of iterative computation, which connects naturally to latent reasoning, adaptive compute, and early exit. Also, the choice of training-time depth distribution likely shapes the quality/compute Pareto frontier at inference. There is still room to optimize that interface.

recommendation.zh: 如果你认真看 looped/shared-depth，这篇该立刻进复现实验：它不是又一个“能训起来”的经验 patch，而是把不稳定性钉到谱范数上，先看稳定性分析和 ablation。
recommendation.en: If you are serious about looped or shared-depth models, this should go straight into your internal repro queue: it is not another empirical patch, but a stability story pinned to spectral norms—read the analysis and ablations first.

paper.title: Design Conditions for Intra-Group Learning of Sequence-Level Rewards: Token Gradient Cancellation

summary.core_problem: 在稀疏终止奖励下，基于 intra-group 比较（同一输入采样多条轨迹、做相对比较）的序列级 RL 微调常出现长期训练不稳定：学习税（有效更新累积失败）、等价解概率漂移、熵塌陷。论文从 token-level credit assignment 出发提出一个必要设计条件：目标函数必须在梯度层面保持 token 更新的“交换性/可交换权重”（gradient exchangeability），使得与奖励弱相关但高频的 token 能在组内发生梯度抵消（cancellation）；否则“非抵消”将成为结构性常态并导致可预测的漂移与塌陷。
summary.importance: 对 RL pretrain / reasoning RL 的启发点是把很多“看起来像超参/噪声问题”的训练退化，归因到目标函数结构是否允许组内对弱信用 token 的梯度抵消。它提供了一个可检验的必要条件与分析框架，可用于审视常见 intra-group 目标（如各种相对优势、组内归一化、片段选择/剪枝）为什么会系统性诱发 reward-irrelevant drift，并提示设计上应尽量保持 token 权重在组内的对称/交换结构。
summary.technical_approach:
作者建立统一形式：组内多轨迹目标可写成对每条轨迹每个 token 的梯度加权和，其中有效权重 ω_{i,t}(τ_i;θ) 与组内比较信号 Â_i 共同决定更新。提出“组内抵消”概念：当某 timestep 上所有轨迹共享同一 (context, token) 且该 token 不携带区分轨迹好坏的信用信息时，理想情况下该 token 的组内聚合梯度应为 0；若由于权重不可交换（non-exchangeable）导致聚合梯度非零，则会对该 context 下的 token 分布产生严格正的 KL 漂移（用 Fisher 信息二阶展开证明），形成学习税与熵塌陷。
论文进一步指出两类常见机制会破坏交换性：1）sequence-coupled 的轨迹聚合（例如把序列级系数耦合到 token 权重并 stop-gradient），2）非对称的 segment pruning/selection（不同轨迹被剪掉/保留的 token 段不一致），使得弱信用 token 的更新系数带上轨迹级随机偏置，从而无法在组内抵消。
在此基础上，作者提出“最小 intra-group 变换”来恢复或近似恢复抵消结构（不改变 intra-group 框架本身），以减少 reward-irrelevant drift。
summary.experiments:
给出的全文片段以理论推导为主：
- 形式化定义了事件 E_{t*}（组内轨迹在某 timestep 共享同一 context-token），并证明若该处聚合梯度 g_{t*}≠0 且 Fisher 在该方向非退化，则一次更新会导致该 context 下分布的严格正 KL 漂移。
- 还给出关于“等价输出 y_a,y_b 在相同奖励下的 log-odds 漂移可跨 K 步累积并趋于 0/∞、导致二元子集熵→0”的结论（在特定 sequence-coupled 线性段更新形式下）。
- 但在所提供内容中，尚未看到具体任务、模型规模、训练步数、指标曲线等实证数字；若全文后半包含实验，应重点核对其是否验证：交换性破坏→漂移/熵塌陷的可预测性，以及提出的最小变换能否在长期训练中维持熵与性能。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议：
- 先读“Necessary Conditions…”一节的定义与命题（尤其是 E_{t*}、组内聚合梯度、Fisher 二阶展开推 KL 漂移），把 exchangeability/cancellation 的判据搞清楚（约 20–30 分钟）。
- 再定位作者点名的两类“破坏交换性”的机制，映射到你熟悉的 RLHF/RLAIF/GRPO 类实现细节（stop-gradient、组内归一化、剪枝/截断）。
- 最后快速看“minimal transformations”部分（若在全文后续），判断它们是否只是对称化/重加权，还是能在不牺牲学习信号的情况下恢复抵消。
预计阅读时间：45–90 分钟（若包含大量实验则更久）。

summary_en.core_problem: In RL fine-tuning with sparse terminal rewards, intra-group comparison objectives (multiple trajectories per prompt, learned via relative ranking/advantages) often become unstable in long training, exhibiting learning tax (ineffective update accumulation), probability drift among reward-equivalent solutions, and entropy collapse. The paper asks for a structural explanation: what necessary design condition must an intra-group objective satisfy at the token-credit level to avoid reward-irrelevant drift? The proposed answer is that token-level gradient exchangeability is necessary so that weak-credit/high-frequency tokens can cancel within the group; otherwise non-cancellation becomes the norm and drift/collapse are inevitable.
summary_en.importance: The main value for RL-pretrain / reasoning-RL practitioners is a diagnostic lens that attributes common long-run failures to objective structure rather than mere noise or hyperparameters. It provides a checkable necessary condition (exchangeability enabling cancellation) that can be used to audit popular intra-group objectives and implementation tricks (sequence-coupled weighting, stop-gradient, asymmetric pruning/selection). It also suggests that stabilizing long-horizon RL may require preserving symmetry in token updates so generic tokens do not accumulate biased gradients.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The paper writes a broad class of intra-group objectives as a sum of token gradients weighted by effective coefficients ω_{i,t}(τ_i;θ) and an intra-group comparison signal Â_i. It formalizes intra-group cancellation: at a timestep where all trajectories share the same (context, token) and that token carries no distinguishing credit, the aggregated group gradient for that token should be zero (or approximately so). If exchangeability is broken and the aggregated gradient is non-zero, the update induces a strictly positive KL drift in the conditional token distribution at that context.
The key proof uses a second-order Taylor expansion of KL around the update and identifies the Hessian with the conditional Fisher information; if g_{t*}≠0 and Fisher is non-degenerate along g_{t*}, then KL increases for sufficiently small step size—i.e., reward-irrelevant drift is guaranteed.
The paper then argues that two common design patterns structurally break exchangeability: (1) sequence-coupled trajectory aggregation with stop-gradient on sequence-level coefficients, and (2) asymmetric segment pruning/selection across trajectories. Finally, it proposes minimal intra-group transformations intended to restore or approximate the cancellation structure without abandoning intra-group comparison learning.
summary_en.experiments:
From the provided full-text portion, the contribution is primarily theoretical:
- A formal condition and theorem: if, under event E_{t*} (shared context-token across the group), the aggregated gradient is non-zero and Fisher is non-degenerate, then the update causes strictly positive conditional KL drift.
- A further result sketches how log-odds between reward-equivalent outputs can drift monotonically over K updates under a sequence-coupled linear-segment update form, driving entropy to 0 on an equivalent subset.
- No concrete empirical setup (tasks, model sizes, curves, numeric gains) is visible in the excerpt; if the full paper includes experiments, they should be checked for (a) predictability of drift under exchangeability violations and (b) whether the proposed minimal transformations prevent entropy collapse while retaining reward learning.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim plan:
- Read the “Necessary Conditions…” section carefully for definitions (E_{t*}, aggregated gradient, conditional Fisher) and the KL-drift proof; this is the conceptual core (20–30 minutes).
- Then scan the parts identifying which practical mechanisms break exchangeability and map them to your RLHF/GRPO-style implementations (stop-gradient, group normalization, truncation/pruning).
- Finally, skim the proposed minimal transformations and evaluate whether they are simple symmetrizations/reweightings or genuinely preserve learning signal while enabling cancellation.
Estimated time: 45–90 minutes depending on how extensive the experimental section is.

recommendation.zh: 读必要条件“token 梯度可交换→组内抵消”那段就够：它把熵塌陷/漂移从超参问题变成目标函数结构问题，适合拿来审你自己的 GRPO 变体。
recommendation.en: Only read the section deriving token-gradient exchangeability/cancellation: it reframes entropy collapse and drift as objective-structure bugs, a sharp lens to audit your own GRPO-style losses.

paper.title: Parcae: Scaling Laws For Stable Looped Language Models

summary.core_problem: 解决 looped / recurrent-depth Transformer（通过在中间层循环同一组 block 来增加 FLOPs 而不增加参数）训练不稳定的问题（residual explosion、loss spikes），并进一步建立“循环次数（looping）作为独立 scaling 轴”的训练 FLOP scaling law 与测试时 compute scaling 规律，使其成为可预测、可控的算力扩展手段。
summary.importance:
这是少见把“架构稳定性（动力系统/谱半径）→ 可训练性 → scaling law”串成闭环的工作，对预训练研究的影响主要在三点：
1) 提供一种在不增参条件下扩展训练 FLOPs 的正交维度（looping），对参数受限/部署受限场景（edge、推理成本占比上升）很关键。
2) 给出 looped 模型不稳定的可解释根因（注入/残差更新矩阵的谱范数过大），并用结构化参数化把稳定性“写进参数空间”，减少靠 Post-Norm/玄学超参救火。
3) 把 looping 纳入 scaling law：不仅展示端到端质量可对标更大 Transformer，还给出 FLOP-optimal 下 data 与 looping 的幂律关系，以及测试时循环带来的可预测收益（指数衰减到不可约损失），这对制定训练配方与预算分配有直接指导意义。
summary.technical_approach:
核心思路：把 middle-looped 架构重写为残差流上的非线性时变动力系统，然后在线性化近似下用控制理论判定发散条件，最后据此设计稳定参数化与训练算法。

1) 动力系统表述：将循环深度的残差更新写成 h_{t+1}=\overline{A} h_t + \overline{B} e + \overline{R}(h_t,e)（文中符号为 \overline{\bm{A}}, \overline{\bm{B}}, \overline{\mathcal{R}}），其中 \overline{A} 控制“保留旧残差 vs 注入新残差”的比例，\overline{B} 将输入表征 e 注入残差流，\overline{R} 吸收注意力/MLP 等非线性模块。

2) 线性化诊断：去掉非线性项得到 LTI 系统，用经典稳定性条件（与 \overline{A} 的谱范数/谱半径相关）解释 residual explosion：既有 looped 架构会学到谱范数过大的注入/更新参数，导致残差随循环步数发散；作者用实证（如 Table 2）展示该现象与训练崩溃/损失尖峰相关。

3) Parcae 架构稳定化：
- 关键结构约束：显式使用连续形式的 A 并做离散化（discretization），再将 A 参数化为“负的对角矩阵”（negative diagonal），从参数空间层面约束谱范数，保证循环更新收缩，从而避免 residual explosion。
- 训练后期 loss spikes 修复：对输入 e 引入额外 normalization（文中称对 e 的归一化），经验上抑制后期尖峰。
- 训练算法修复：原训练目标是对“随机深度/循环次数”的期望损失做最小化；作者提出 intra-batch per-sequence depth sampling（同一 batch 内不同样本采不同循环深度）以降低梯度方差/减少 loss spikes，并改善可扩展训练稳定性。

4) Scaling law 建模：在参数匹配、isoFLOP 设定下，比较“增加数据”与“增加循环次数”两种提升训练 FLOPs 的方式，拟合 FLOP-optimal 下 data 与 looping 的幂律；并在测试时研究循环次数增加带来的 loss 改善呈指数衰减并趋于不可约项，最后把训练与测试两类规律合并成统一 scaling 公式。
summary.experiments:
论文在引言给出关键数字与设置：
- 端到端质量：对比参数/数据匹配的 RDMs（Recurrent Depth Models，looped 基线）与标准 Transformer。相对 RDM，Parcae 将验证集 PPL 降低 6.3%。
- 大规模结果：当扩展到 1.3B 参数、100B tokens 训练时，Parcae 在 Core 与 Core-Extended 基准上分别比参数匹配 Transformer 高最多 2.99 与 1.18 分，并能“匹配最多两倍参数量的 Transformer”。
- 稳定性：文中声称通过谱约束避免 residual explosion，并通过 e-normalization 与 intra-batch 深度采样减少训练后期 loss spikes（具体量化需在正文表格/曲线中核对）。
- Scaling：给出 looping 作为正交轴的训练 FLOP scaling（Figure 1 右）以及测试时 compute scaling 的指数衰减规律（需结合正文拟合曲线与不可约损失项的估计方式理解）。
summary.reading_guide:
精读建议（建议 2–3 小时，带着复现/迁移的目的）：
1) Section 1 + 动力系统公式（Eq.1）：弄清 \overline{A}/\overline{B}/\overline{R} 分别对应到 Transformer 残差路径的哪些参数（尤其是“injection parameters”具体指什么）。
2) 线性化与稳定性推导：重点看从非线性时变系统到 LTI 的近似假设、稳定性条件如何落到谱范数约束，以及该条件与实际训练崩溃现象（Table 2）如何对应。
3) Parcae 的 A 离散化与 negative diagonal 参数化：这是核心创新之一。建议对照实现细节理解：为何选对角、为何必须为负、离散化形式（如 Euler/指数映射类）对稳定域的影响。
4) 两个“工程但关键”的稳定化：e 的 normalization、intra-batch per-sequence depth sampling。建议看消融：分别去掉会发生什么、是否与 batch size/学习率/优化器强相关。
5) Scaling law 部分：
- 训练侧：isoFLOP 下 data vs looping 的幂律拟合方法、误差条与外推稳定性；
- 测试侧：指数衰减到不可约损失的拟合与解释；
- 统一公式：如何把训练与测试规律组合用于预算分配（训练 loops、训练 tokens、推理 loops）。

summary_en.core_problem: Stabilize training of looped (recurrent-depth) language models—where compute is scaled by iterating a shared block rather than adding parameters—by eliminating residual-stream explosion and loss spikes, and then establish predictable scaling laws where looping becomes an orthogonal axis for both training-FLOP scaling and test-time compute scaling.
summary_en.importance: Parcae is valuable to foundation-model pretraining because it connects three usually separate threads into one actionable recipe: (i) a mechanistic instability diagnosis (dynamical systems + spectral conditions), (ii) an architecture that bakes stability into parameterization (rather than relying on fragile norms/hyperparameters), and (iii) empirical scaling laws showing looping can substitute for parameters/data under isoFLOP constraints and can be used for test-time compute scaling with predictable returns. This directly informs how to allocate budgets when parameters are capped (deployment memory) but FLOPs are available (training or inference).
summary_en.technical_approach:
1) Dynamical-systems reframing: middle-looped transformers are written as a nonlinear time-varying dynamical system over the residual stream, with matrices controlling state carryover (\overline{A}), input injection (\overline{B}), and a nonlinear operator (\overline{R}) subsuming attention/MLP modules.

2) Linearized stability analysis: by linearizing (dropping \overline{R}), the update becomes an LTI system, enabling classic control-theory reasoning: divergence/residual explosion occurs when the effective state-update has too large a spectral norm. The authors argue prior looped recipes can learn such unstable \overline{A}-like injection parameterizations, empirically correlating with training blow-ups and loss spikes.

3) Parcae architecture: they introduce an explicit continuous-time representation A, discretize it, and parameterize A as a negative diagonal matrix. This constrains the spectrum to be contractive, preventing residual explosion by construction.

4) Training stabilizers for loss spikes: (i) an additional normalization on the input representation e to mitigate late-stage spikes, and (ii) a modified stochastic-depth objective implementation via intra-batch per-sequence depth sampling, reducing spike frequency/variance when optimizing expected loss over variable loop counts.

5) Scaling-law modeling: under parameter-matched isoFLOP comparisons, they fit FLOP-optimal power laws showing data and looping should co-increase; at test time, increasing recurrence yields predictable exponential decay toward an irreducible loss, and they combine train-time and test-time laws into a unified scaling relation for looped models.
summary_en.experiments:
Key reported numbers from the paper’s main text:
- End-to-end quality: vs parameter/data-matched RDM baselines, Parcae reduces validation perplexity by 6.3%.
- Large-scale run: at 1.3B parameters trained on 100B tokens, Parcae beats parameter-matched standard Transformers by up to +2.99 (Core) and +1.18 (Core-Extended), and matches Transformers up to ~2× larger.
- Stability: they report eliminating residual explosion (linked to spectral issues) and reducing late-stage loss spikes via e-normalization and intra-batch depth sampling (confirm exact spike metrics/plots in the experiments section).
- Scaling: they provide empirical power laws for FLOP-optimal training where looping is an orthogonal axis, and test-time scaling curves consistent with exponential decay to an irreducible loss (see Figure 1 right and the test-time scaling section).
summary_en.reading_guide:
Deep-read checklist (2–3 hours):
- The dynamical-system formulation and the mapping from transformer components to \overline{A}/\overline{B}/\overline{R} (this determines how general the stability claim is).
- The linearization assumptions and the exact spectral condition used to argue instability; cross-check with the empirical residual-explosion evidence (e.g., Table 2).
- The discretization choice and the negative-diagonal parameterization of A: why diagonal, why negative, and what stability region it guarantees.
- The two spike mitigations (e-normalization, intra-batch per-sequence depth sampling) and their ablations—these are likely to matter in real pretraining pipelines.
- Scaling-law methodology: isoFLOP setup, fitting procedure, confidence intervals, and how the unified train+test scaling law can be used to choose (tokens, loops) during training and (loops) at inference.

recommendation.zh: 把looped深度循环的失稳根因用谱半径讲清并给出“写进参数化”的稳定方案，还顺手给了可用的looping scaling law；值得按其稳定化手段做一次干净ablation再决定是否上生产配方。
recommendation.en: They pin looped-depth instability to spectral-radius issues and bake stability into the parameterization, then provide usable looping scaling laws; worth running a clean ablation with their stabilization trick before betting on looping as a production recipe.
